response:
Woman: A case report
A 67-year-old woman with no obvious symptoms presented to our hospital in November 2012. She was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (postacute leukemia) and identified with LCH after diagnosis. After chemotherapy and radiation, LCH returned, and she was finally referred to orthopedics for a physical examination. X-ray showed a mass at the anterior end of C1. The magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed the existence of the subchondral sclerosis at the base of the C1 cervical vertebrae, especially between the vertebrae and the atlas and the mass did not affect the neurological function at all. In this article we aim to describe a difficult case of a middle-aged woman with Langerhans histiocytosis involving the cervical spine that may be of benefit to other histocystoid individuals.
